newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline stable as NYMEX rebounds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline stable as NYMEX rebounds.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices were stable Thursday, supported by higher product futures markets, traders said.
By 12 PST, unleaded gasoline for May delivery rose 0.64 cents a gallon on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).
The price for California-grade wholesale gasoline, which tracked NYMEX by falling 7.8 percent Wednesday, was seen stable around 76 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, traders said.
Conventional gasoline, for sale outside the state, held at 68/69 cents, traders said.
Yesterday's slide could resume next week, traders said, with crude prices cheap relative to West Coast products, which refiners could exploit by selling crack spreads.
"Some of them are selling...They're figuring its a darn good crack spread," one trader said.
The trader figured a barrel of California conventional gasoline earns a profit of roughly $9 in the current crude futures market.
